lifecycle.reason: A failed load returns before a value exists. After a successful load, the entry frees a returned dump string and decrements the loaded value; the loader closes its lexer and the dump functions close their temporary buffers and parent set.

control_flow.reason: Both dump modes are guarded by successful json_loadb. Parsing rejects nesting beyond JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH, while dumping starts at depth zero and rejects only when its recursion reaches that limit. The entry has no construction step that can pass an over-depth value to a dump call.

accepted.requirement: The JSON dump operation must be able to receive a supported, over-depth json_t so its clean depth-limit failure can be exercised.
accepted.target_route: A finite command prefix can select either dump mode and carry nested JSON bytes. The entry calls json_loadb first, returns on NULL, and passes only its successful result to json_dumps or json_dump_callback.
accepted.failure_condition: An object with a child at dump depth JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH reaches do_dump's new failure guard when separately constructed, but JSON text that would yield such an object requires a parse_value call beyond the parser's maximum depth. json_loadb returns NULL before either dump call.
accepted.alternative_paths: JSON_DECODE_ANY affects the accepted root type and JSON_DISABLE_EOF_CHECK affects trailing input; neither bypasses parse_value's depth guard. Both dump modes use the same loaded object. The complete entry contains no object-construction or mutation route after loading.
